I will read four files before I edit anything. I do not have the current skill text or the two guides in view, so an edit now would be a guess.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Your baseline shows the "agent knows the rule and skips it under pressure" failure. For this type, the writing-skills guide calls for a firm prohibition, a rationalization table, and a red flags list. A rationalization table pairs each excuse with its counter. A red flags list names the thoughts that signal a skip is near. Soft wording like "prefer" is the wrong form here.
- Your three quotes are three different excuses. "It's only a patch release" claims an exemption. "I'll run it right after tagging" claims the order does not matter. "The spirit is a good changelog" claims the letter does not matter. Each needs its own counter.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

My plan after the reads:

1. Add counters only for the excuses in the baseline. I will not add cases for excuses we have not seen.
2. Check the `description` field. It should list the symptoms that mean "use this skill now". It should not summarize the workflow.
3. Re-run the same 15 scenarios with the edited skill. I will report how many runs still tag without the check.
4. Add a counter for each new excuse that appears, then re-run.

I will not commit anything. Tell me if you want a different scope.
